key_insight: A composite nonsmooth nonconvex problem with a convex regularizer can be solved with the same optimal oracle complexity as the noncomposite case by extending online-to-nonconvex conversion.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretically optimal template for training constrained or regularized large-scale models when only stochastic gradients or function values are available.
method: Use an online learner to generate update directions for nonconvex optimization.
Modify the online losses so the convex regularizer appears directly rather than via linearization.
Apply a low-regret online mirror descent variant to obtain Goldstein-type stationarity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The paper proves oracle-complexity rates of O(δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) stochastic gradient queries or O(dδ^{-1}ε^{-3}) function-value queries, and reports numerical experiments plus smooth-case rates.
watch_item: The guarantees are worst-case and depend on the Goldstein radius δ and stationarity tolerance ε, so practical performance may vary with parameter tuning and problem conditioning.
paper_title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity
